Literature', one 17:01Z snapshot, pytest 275 passed, finals sha unchanged 1f1ddb6d/a77bcd6b/55038fd6, claude grep 0, API SELECTED 2/2 at 20:04:35Z, poller fresh. Its static gate passes, all 4 sources are listable, and HF v3's author CSV is byte-identical to our exp56 x138 dummy (sha d52a5da2), so the pipeline is deterministic. The full gate with exp56 as a stand-in passes. The dry kernel was COMPLETE by 20:34:26Z. Its run took 19.5 min (log 1169 s; clips 44b6_0113de3b 975.7 s, 44b6_0b24845f 1031.8 s, 6bba_05b6850b 1043.0 s, 6bba_05db0fb1 1147.3 s kernel_elapsed), so push to COMPLETE took ~32 min. The output fetch with --file-pattern was blocked by HTTP 429 from 20:34Z to 20:41Z (PC12-11). The full gate (--pulled dry_2026-09-26 --port exp63dry_hfv3 --dummy <dry output> --author <HF v3 output> --version 5) gives RESULT PASS, exit 0, 0 FAIL and 0 SKIP lines. Our dummy CSV sha256 d52a5da2 == the author CSV == the exp56 dummy CSV (121,219 nodes, 62 forks), and the log shows the validator disabled with no DEADLINE, sweep or rewrite lines. Fixes proposed: (1) fetch outputs with --file-pattern (16 s vs 216 s / 52 MB); (2) E10 v2 'first seen' cannot be recorded from snapshots (no version field), and a morning OK would exclude any overnight successor, so the user needs to answer tonight; (3) until 27 Sep 11:30Z, P1 depends only on the research-round chain, so re-arm the timer to act on snapshot age; (4) a morning reminder before the v2 lapse at 12:00Z; (5) a new RESUME POINT plus a fix to the stale MEMORY index line; (6) a mis-submit guard for the dry-run id and unique slugs for a second port; (7) at a trigger, only one process calls `kernels output`, with a 2-minute back-off on HTTP 429 (measured today: a ~6 min block). No rule violations were found. No new mechanism can pass R8, and the finals stay #37 + #38.

findings.what: Measured: the author-output fetch in the E10 procedure is 13x slower than it needs to be. A plain `kaggle kernels output raunakdey07/biohub-harmonic-fusion-v3` downloads 52 MB (tracking_repo/, secondary_seed_weights/, edge_cache/, jsonl files) in 216 s. The same applies to fetching our own dummy's output.

findings.what: E10 v2 V2 ('only a successor first seen (ref + version in an e10_watch snapshot or on its page) after the OK time') cannot be applied mechanically for two reasons. (a) The snapshots record no version: tools/e10_snapshot.py stores only ref, title, author, lastRunTime and totalVotes. The page shows the LAST SUCCESSFUL version, not the latest (redteam: amanatar page 'Version 1 of 5', anhad 'Version 6 of 9'). (b) Timing: every research round writes a snapshot overnight. If the user answers only in the morning, any 0.954-0.955 successor that a round snapshot saw overnight is excluded from v2 permanently (v1 still covers >= 0.956). The overnight burst (~07-09Z) is the most likely window for such a successor. So an answer tonight and an answer tomorrow morning are not equivalent.

findings.what: Night-time mis-submit guard. The dry kernel id vitaliineibauer/biohub-exp63-succ-dryrun-raunakdey07 matches the gate's PORT_ID_PREFIX 'vitaliineibauer/biohub-exp63-succ-', so the gate passes it (suffix mismatch = INFO), and the ledger regex exp63[a-z]* maps it to x138. During an unattended night trigger (P8/V7), a wrong kernel ref in `kaggle competitions submit -k` would pass every automated check. Also, V5 allows a second port, and a second successor by the same author would collide on the P4 slug 'biohub-exp63-succ-<author>': pushing it creates version 2 of the first port's kernel.

findings.what: Measured during this round: the Kaggle API rate-limits output downloads per account. `kaggle kernels output` (endpoint ListKernelSessionOutput) returned HTTP 429 Too Many Requests on 4 tries from 20:34:5xZ to 20:38:51Z and worked again at 20:41:06Z, so it was blocked for ~6 min. Before the 429 there were about 3-5 output calls in ~30 min from parallel agents (this agent 2 fetches of HF v3, the redteam agent at least 1, possibly the main session). `kernels status` kept working during the block. At a real trigger the procedure needs 2 output fetches (the author's and our dummy's). If round agents or a second session call `kernels output` at the same time, the gate can stall for minutes. That eats into V3's 01:45Z margin and into the port's place inside the copy block.

findings.action: Mechanical, for the E10 command sequence: (1) only the session running the port calls `kernels output` during a trigger, and research or browser agents never do; (2) fetch the author's output right after the static gate, while our dummy is still queued, so the two fetches are ~30 min apart; (3) on a 429, retry every 2 min for up to 20 min and log each try, and if the limit persists, notify and wait (the strict P8 default); (4) poll status no more often than every 2-3 min (status calls were not limited, but they are the same API family).
